read.ko: 우리는 아직 우리 자신을 세계 시민이라고 생각하지 않을 수도 있지만, 그렇게 생각하는 것은 필요하면서도 가능하기도 하다.
read.en: We might not think of ourselves as global citizens yet, but it’s both necessary and possible to do so.

read.ko: 어떤 사람들은 세계 시민이라는 개념에 대해 회의적이지만, 인류 역사 대부분의 기간 동안 사람들은 자기 자신을 국민 국가의 시민이라고 생각하지 않았 다.
read.en: Some people are skeptical about the idea of global citizenship, but for most of human history, people didn’t think of themselves as citizens of nation-states.

read.ko: 어쨌든, 인류 역사 대부분의 기간 동안 국민 국가는 존재하지 않았다.
read.en: After all, for most of human history, nation-states didn’t exist.

read.ko: 지난 몇 세기에 걸친 국민 국가의 부상은 사람들로 하여금 가족, 민족 집단, 혹은 종교와 같은 다른 정체성들에 국가 시민 정체성을 더하게 만들었다.
read.en: The rise of nation-states over the last few centuries has led people to add state citizenship to other identities, such as family, people group, or religion.

read.ko: 전 세계 사람들 간의 연결과 우리가 직면한 공통 과제들을 고려할 때, 우리는 이러한 다른 정체성들 위에 세계 시민 정체성을 쌓을 필요가 있다.
read.en: Given the connections between people around the world and the common challenges we face, we need to layer global citizenship on to these other identities.

read.ko: 이것이 세계 시민 정체성이 이러한 다른 정체성들을 대체한다는 것을 의미하지는 않는다.
read.en: This doesn’t mean that global citizenship replaces these other identities.

read.ko: 우리의 정체성들에 관한 단 하나의 이야기가 있는 것은 아니다.
read.en: There’s not a single story about our identities.

read.ko: 오히려, 그것은 정확하게는 우리가 우리의 가족, 공동체 내의 사람들, ‘그리고’ 전 세계 사람들에 대한 의무를 지니고 있기 때문이다.
read.en: Instead, it’s precisely because we have obligations to our families, those in our community, and those around the world.

read.ko: 만족하지 못하는 직업인들 사이에는 되풀이해서 나타나는 주제가 있다. 그것은 언젠가 (미래의 알 수 없는 날에) 상황이 기적적으로 바뀌어 자신들이 우연 히 완벽한 일자리나 경력을 마주칠 것이라는 믿음이다.
read.en: Among unsatisfied professionals, there’s a repeating theme — the belief that someday (a mysterious day in the future) things will miraculously change and they’ll stumble into the perfect job or career.

read.ko: 그러면서도 그들은 (대체로) 자신의 현재 상황을 의미 있게 바꾸기 위해 하는 일이 거의 없다.
read.en: At the same time, they (typically) do little to meaningfully alter their current situation.

read.ko: 그들은 자신의 일자리를 좋아하지 않는데, 그래서 그들은 무엇을 하는가?
read.en: They don’t like their job, so what do they do?

read.ko: 그들은 구인란으로 가서 비슷한 직책의 일자리를 검색하고, 다른 부서나 회사에서 그저 새로 고침 버튼만 누르면 우주가 자신의 경력에 약간의 마법 가루 를 뿌려 주기를 바란다.
read.en: They head to job boards and search for roles with a similar job title, hoping that the universe will sprinkle a bit of magic on their career if they just hit the refresh button in a different department or company.

read.ko: 이와 같은 노력은 직업인들로 하여금 자신들이 무언가를 하고 있는 것처럼 느끼게 하지만, 실제로 그들은 단지 새로운 일자리를 구한 뒤 이전에 그랬던 것 처럼 빠르게 환상이 깨질 상황에 스스로를 처하게 할 뿐이다.
read.en: Efforts like this make professionals feel like they are doing something, when really they’re just setting themselves up to take a new role and quickly become just as disenchanted as they were before.

read.ko: 이는 타이타닉호의 갑판 의자들을 재배치하는 것과 같다.
read.en: It’s like rearranging deck chairs on the Titanic.

read.ko: 여러분은 자신의 접근 방식을 완전히 바꾸어야 한다.
read.en: You’ve got to completely switch up your approach.

read.ko: 여러분이 계속해서 같은 게임을 한다면, 똑같은 보상을 얻게 될 것이다.
read.en: If you keep playing the same game, you’ll win the same prizes.

read.ko: 사회학자들은 시간에 대한 우리의 인식과 시간 사용이 배경에서 째깍거리며 흘러가는 시계처럼 단순히 자연의 기본적인 속성도 아니고, 단순히 개인적 경 험의 심리적 현상도 아니라고 주장한다.
read.en: Sociologists argue that our perception and usage of time are not just basic properties of nature, like a clock ticking away in the background, nor are they simply psychological phenomena of individual experience.

read.ko: 오히려 우리가 시간을 인식하고 이해하는 방식은 상당한 정도로 전통과 문화적 기준에 의해 형성된다.
read.en: Instead, how we perceive and understand time is to a large degree shaped by tradition and cultural norms.

read.ko: Eviatar Zerubavel의 저서인 『The Seven Day Circle: The History and Meaning of the Week』는 시간의 기본 단위인 일주일이 어떻게 사람들이 그들 의 활동과 삶의 리듬을 구조화하는 방식에 영향을 끼치면서 문화마다 다른 사회적 발명품인지를 보여 준다.
read.en: Eviatar Zerubavel’s work, The Seven Day Circle: The History and Meaning of the Week, demonstrates how the week, a fundamental unit of time, is a social invention that varies across cultures, influencing how people structure their activities and rhythms of life.

read.ko: 왜 우리는 9시부터 5시까지 일하는 직업을 일상적인 것으로 여기는가?
read.en: Why do we consider a nine-to-five job routine?

read.ko: 왜 우리 중 많은 사람은 주말마다 일하지 않는가?
read.en: Why don’t many of us work on the weekends?

read.ko: 왜 우리는 대개 월말에 고지 금액을 납부하는가?
read.en: Why do we usually pay our bills at the end of the month?

read.ko: 왜 은퇴 연령은 65세인가?
read.en: Why is the retirement age sixty-five?

read.ko: 이러한 숫자와 양식은 실제로 자연이나 인간의 어떤 본질적인 특성에 의해 좌우되는 것이 아니라, 오히려 우리가 내면화하여 결국 ‘기준’으로 받아들이게 된 사회적 창조물이다.
read.en: These numbers and patterns aren’t really dictated by nature or any essential human characteristic, but are rather social creations that we internalize and come to accept as “normal.”

read.ko: 최근 몇 년 동안 특히 기업 차원에서 발생하는 위법 행위의 수가 증가했거나, 적어도 세상에 드러난 사건의 수가 증가했다.
read.en: In recent years, the number of illegal actions in particular at the corporate level has grown, or at least the number of cases that came to light, increased.

read.ko: 그러한 위법 행위는 용기 있는 제보자들이 그것을 끝내기 위해 많은 위험을 무릅써 왔기 때문에 비로소 종종 드러났다.
read.en: Such misconduct has often only been exposed because brave informants have risked a great deal in order to put an end to it.

read.ko: 따라서 내부 고발자 보호가 주목받게 된 것은 놀라운 일이 아니다.
read.en: Hence, it is no surprise that whistleblower protection has come into focus.

read.ko: 기업의 직원들이 보복이나 불이익을 두려워하여 위법 행위를 신고하기를 꺼려서 법과 질서의 위반이 여러 해 동안 적발되지도 처벌받지도 않는다면, 그것 은 여러 가지 부정적인 영향을 미칠 수 있다.
read.en: If violations of law and order go undetected and unpunished for years because employees of a company fear to report illegal activities for fear of reprisals or consequences, it can have several negative effects.

read.ko: 그것은 해당 기업 자체에 해를 끼칠 수 있지만, 또한 제삼자, 경제 전반, 일반 대중, 심지어 법치주의마저도 영향을 받을 수 있다.
read.en: It can harm the company itself, but also third-parties, the economy in general, the general public, and even the rule of law could be affected.

read.ko: 위법하거나 심지어 범죄인 행위를 줄이는 데 도움을 주려는 사람들을 보호하는 것은 두 가지 주요 기능을 지닌다. 즉, 그 사람의 행위를 보호하는 것과 공 익을 보호하는 것이다.
read.en: Protecting those who would assist in reducing unlawful or even criminal behaviour has two main functions: Protecting the individual’s actions as well as protecting the public good.

read.ko: 균형이 잘 잡힌 내부 고발자 보호는 이 두 가지 모두에 긍정적인 영향을 미칠 수 있다.
read.en: A well-balanced whistleblower protection may have positive effects on both of these.

read.ko: 안타깝게도 목표에 대한 상상은 때때로 그것을 달성하기 위해 요구되는 것의 일상적인 현실로부터 동떨어져 있다.
read.en: Unfortunately, sometimes the idea of a goal is disconnected from the daily reality of what it will take to achieve it.

read.ko: 우리는 목표에 대한 ‘상상’과 사랑에 빠져, 우리가 그것을 실현하기 위해서 우리의 하루하루가 얼마나 달라져야 할지를 생각에서 밀어낸다.
read.en: We fall in love with the idea of a goal, pushing out of mind how different our day-to-day will need to be for us to make it happen.

read.ko: 실제로, 연구는 심지어 우리의 환상이 우리에게 거짓되고 때 이른 성취감을 주기 때문에 우리의 미래에 대한 긍정적 환상이 우리가 우리의 목표에 노력을 ‘덜’ 기울이게 할 수 있다는 것을 시사한다.
read.en: In fact, research even suggests that positive fantasies about our future can lead us to put less effort into our goals because our fantasies provide us with a false and premature sense of accomplishment.

read.ko: 우리는 목표를 낭만화한다. 즉, 변화에 대한 상상과 사랑에 빠진다.
read.en: We romanticize a goal — falling in love with the idea of a change.

read.ko: 그 과정에서 우리는 복잡한 새로운 행동을 우리의 삶에 통합하는 것의 복잡함과 어려움에 대해 얼버무리고 넘어간다.
read.en: In the process, we gloss over the intricacies and challenges of integrating a complex new behavior into our life.

read.ko: 한 연구가 이를 잘 요약했듯이, 긍정적인 미래에 대하여 환상을 품는 것은 “사람을 현혹시켜 원하는 미래를 지금 여기에서 머릿속으로 즐기게 한다.”
read.en: As one study nicely summed it up, fantasizing about a positive future “seduces a person to mentally enjoy the desired future in the here and now” —

read.ko: 그래서 우리가 우리의 환상이 아직 우리의 미래가 아닌 ‘이유’에 대해 돌아보지 않기 때문에 “행동해야 할 필요가 유발되지 않는다.”
read.en: and because we don’t reflect on why our fantasy is not yet our future, “a necessity to act is not induced.”

para.en: We might not think of ourselves as global citizens yet, but it’s both necessary and possible to do so. Some people are skeptical about the idea of global citizenship, but for most of human history, people didn’t think of themselves as citizens of nation-states. After all, for most of human history, nation-states didn’t exist. The rise of nation-states over the last few centuries has led people to add state citizenship to other identities, such as family, people group, or religion. Given the connections between people around the world and the common challenges we face, we need to layer global citizenship on to these other identities. This doesn’t mean that global citizenship replaces these other identities. There’s not a single story about our identities. Instead, it’s precisely because we have obligations to our families, those in our community, and those around the world.

Among unsatisfied professionals, there’s a repeating theme — the belief that someday (a mysterious day in the future) things will miraculously change and they’ll stumble into the perfect job or career. At the same time, they (typically) do little to meaningfully alter their current situation. They don’t like their job, so what do they do? They head to job boards and search for roles with a similar job title, hoping that the universe will sprinkle a bit of magic on their career if they just hit the refresh button in a different department or company. Efforts like this make professionals feel like they are doing something, when really they’re just setting themselves up to take a new role and quickly become just as disenchanted as they were before. It’s like rearranging deck chairs on the Titanic. You’ve got to completely switch up your approach. If you keep playing the same game, you’ll win the same prizes.

Sociologists argue that our perception and usage of time are not just basic properties of nature, like a clock ticking away in the background, nor are they simply psychological phenomena of individual experience. Instead, how we perceive and understand time is to a large degree shaped by tradition and cultural norms. Eviatar Zerubavel’s work, The Seven Day Circle: The History and Meaning of the Week, demonstrates how the week, a fundamental unit of time, is a social invention that varies across cultures, influencing how people structure their activities and rhythms of life. Why do we consider a nine-to-five job routine? Why don’t many of us work on the weekends? Why do we usually pay our bills at the end of the month? Why is the retirement age sixty-five? These numbers and patterns aren’t really dictated by nature or any essential human characteristic, but are rather social creations that we internalize and come to accept as “normal.”

In recent years, the number of illegal actions in particular at the corporate level has grown, or at least the number of cases that came to light, increased. Such misconduct has often only been exposed because brave informants have risked a great deal in order to put an end to it. Hence, it is no surprise that whistleblower protection has come into focus. If violations of law and order go undetected and unpunished for years because employees of a company fear to report illegal activities for fear of reprisals or consequences, it can have several negative effects. It can harm the company itself, but also third-parties, the economy in general, the general public, and even the rule of law could be affected. Protecting those who would assist in reducing unlawful or even criminal behaviour has two main functions: Protecting the individual’s actions as well as protecting the public good. A well-balanced whistleblower protection may have positive effects on both of these.

Unfortunately, sometimes the idea of a goal is disconnected from the daily reality of what it will take to achieve it. We fall in love with the idea of a goal, pushing out of mind how different our day-to-day will need to be for us to make it happen. In fact, research even suggests that positive fantasies about our future can lead us to put less effort into our goals because our fantasies provide us with a false and premature sense of accomplishment. We romanticize a goal — falling in love with the idea of a change. In the process, we gloss over the intricacies and challenges of integrating a complex new behavior into our life. As one study nicely summed it up, fantasizing about a positive future “seduces a person to mentally enjoy the desired future in the here and now” — and because we don’t reflect on why our fantasy is not yet our future, “a necessity to act is not induced.”
